bios.steps.intel.asrock: BIOS > OC Tweaker: Intel Default profile first.|CPU Configuration > ratio, with tests.

bios.steps.intel.generic: Ratio and power-limit settings are in the BIOS overclocking menus or Intel XTU (K/KF/KS CPUs on Z chipsets).

bios.steps.pbo.asrock: BIOS > OC Tweaker / Advanced > AMD Overclocking > Precision Boost Overdrive.|Light negative Curve Optimizer, then tests.
bios.steps.pbo.asus: BIOS > Ai Tweaker > Precision Boost Overdrive.|Start with PBO "Enabled" without raising limits, then light negative Curve Optimizer (-5 to -10) in steps with tests.
bios.steps.pbo.dell: Dell PCs generally do not expose PBO; on Alienware see Alienware Command Center.
bios.steps.pbo.generic: Look for "Precision Boost Overdrive" in the BIOS AMD Overclocking menus, or use AMD Ryzen Master.
bios.steps.pbo.gigabyte: BIOS > Tweaker > Advanced CPU Settings > Precision Boost Overdrive.|Light negative Curve Optimizer, then tests.
bios.steps.pbo.hp: HP PCs generally do not expose PBO.
bios.steps.pbo.lenovo: Lenovo PCs generally do not expose PBO.
bios.steps.pbo.msi: BIOS > OC > Advanced CPU Configuration > AMD Overclocking > Precision Boost Overdrive.|Curve Optimizer: All Cores, Negative, small value, then tests.
bios.steps.rebar.asrock: BIOS > Advanced > Chipset Configuration: Above 4G Decoding = Enabled, C.A.M. Clever Access Memory = Enabled.|Boot > CSM = Disabled.
bios.steps.rebar.asus: BIOS > Advanced > PCI Subsystem Settings: Above 4G Decoding = Enabled, Re-Size BAR = Auto.|Boot > CSM = Disabled.
bios.steps.rebar.dell: Update the BIOS: on supported models Dell enables Resizable BAR through the BIOS.
bios.steps.rebar.generic: Enable "Above 4G Decoding" and "Resizable BAR / Smart Access Memory" in the BIOS.|Disable CSM (UEFI boot).
bios.steps.rebar.gigabyte: BIOS > Settings > IO Ports: Above 4G Decoding = Enabled, Re-Size BAR Support = Auto.|Boot > CSM Support = Disabled.
bios.steps.rebar.hp: Update the BIOS: on supported models HP enables Resizable BAR through the BIOS.
bios.steps.rebar.lenovo: Update the BIOS: on supported models Lenovo enables Resizable BAR through the BIOS.
bios.steps.rebar.msi: BIOS > Settings > Advanced > PCI Subsystem Settings: Above 4G memory = Enabled, Re-Size BAR Support = Enabled.
bios.steps.xmp.asrock: BIOS (F2) > OC Tweaker > DRAM Configuration.|Load XMP / EXPO Setting: Profile 1.|F10 to save.
bios.steps.xmp.asus: BIOS (Del) > Ai Tweaker (advanced mode F7).|Ai Overclock Tuner: choose XMP I / XMP II (Intel) or EXPO (AMD).|F10 to save, then check stability.
bios.steps.xmp.dell: Dell consumer PCs often do not expose XMP; on Alienware: BIOS (F2) > Overclocking > XMP.
bios.steps.xmp.generic: Enter the BIOS (Del/F2 at boot).|Look for XMP, EXPO, DOCP or "Memory Profile" in overclocking/memory menus.|Pick profile 1, save (F10) and check stability.
bios.steps.xmp.gigabyte: BIOS (Del) > Tweaker.|Extreme Memory Profile (X.M.P.) / EXPO: Profile 1.|F10 to save.
bios.steps.xmp.hp: On OMEN: BIOS (F10) or OMEN Gaming Hub > Performance > Memory. Many HP PCs do not expose XMP.
bios.steps.xmp.lenovo: On Legion: BIOS (F2) or Lenovo Legion Space/Vantage. Many Lenovo PCs do not expose XMP.
bios.steps.xmp.msi: BIOS (Del) > EZ Mode home page: A-XMP / XMP / EXPO button.|Choose Profile 1.|F10 to save.

bios.update.note: FrameCore never downloads or flashes a BIOS. Check on the official page: exact model, board revision (e.g. rev 1.0 / 1.1), release notes, CPU compatibility.
bios.update.risks: A power loss during the update can brick the board.|BIOS settings (XMP/EXPO, fans, PBO) are often reset: note them first.|BitLocker may ask for the recovery key after the update: back it up.|Never flash a file from a third-party site or for another board revision.
bios.update.risks.label: Risks
bios.update.steps.asrock: Download the BIOS from asrock.com (Support > BIOS) for your model.|Copy it to a FAT32 USB drive.|Enter the BIOS (F2) > Tool > Instant Flash.|Alternative: BIOS Flashback if your board has it.
bios.update.steps.asus: Download the BIOS from asus.com (Support > Drivers & Tools > BIOS) for your exact model.|Copy the file to a FAT32 USB drive.|Restart, press Del to enter the BIOS, then Tool > ASUS EZ Flash 3.|Select the file and confirm; do not cut power.|Alternative without CPU/RAM: BIOS FlashBack button (see manual).
bios.update.steps.dell: Use Dell Command | Update or SupportAssist, or download the update from dell.com/support with your service tag.|Plug in the charger (laptop) and run the official executable; the PC restarts to flash.
bios.update.steps.generic: Identify the exact model and board revision (printed on the PCB or the box).|Download the BIOS only from the manufacturer's official site.|Follow the BIOS built-in flash utility described in the manual.
bios.update.steps.gigabyte: Download the BIOS from gigabyte.com (Support > BIOS) for your model AND revision.|Copy it to a FAT32 USB drive.|Enter the BIOS (Del) > Q-Flash (F8), select the file.|Alternative: Q-Flash Plus button (file renamed GIGABYTE.bin).
bios.update.steps.hp: Use HP Support Assistant or download the update from support.hp.com for your model.|Plug in the charger (laptop) and follow the HP wizard; the PC restarts to flash.
bios.update.steps.lenovo: Use Lenovo Vantage / System Update or download the update from pcsupport.lenovo.com.|Plug in the charger (laptop) and run the official tool.
bios.update.steps.msi: Download the BIOS from msi.com (Support > BIOS) for your exact model.|Extract it to a FAT32 USB drive.|Enter the BIOS (Del) > M-Flash, select the file.|Alternative: rear "Flash BIOS" button (file renamed MSI.ROM).
bios.update.title: BIOS update
